source.title: Targeted Memory Reactivation during Sleep Adaptively Promotes the Strengthening or Weakening of Overlapping Memories

confidence_rationale: This is close to the strongest single piece of support in this pull for MECH-529's core empirical signature -- that offline reorganisation is SELECTIVE and RELATIONAL (differentially strengthening or weakening specific overlapping memories based on their associative structure) rather than a uniform consolidation multiplier applied indiscriminately. The study causally reactivates one memory during sleep and shows the ADAPTIVE, bidirectional (strengthen-or-weaken) regulation of associated overlapping memories as a function of their relative associative strength with the shared element -- exactly the split/merge/reweighting signature MECH-529 predicts, in a causally-manipulated (not merely correlational) human sleep paradigm.
failure_signatures: The overlapping-memory structure here is experimenter-defined via explicit shared elements in an associative-learning task (paired-associate learning with deliberately overlapping cues), not discovered from accumulated consequential-divergence evidence the way MECH-529 requires -- the same oracular-structure caveat that applies to the Solomon 2026 entry already in this directory.

The paradigm measures memory strength (recall accuracy) as the readout, not object equivalence-class membership, index continuity, or generalisation behaviour specifically -- MECH-529's non-oracularity and index-continuity requirements are untested here.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Using targeted memory reactivation during sleep to selectively reactivate one memory from a network of associatively overlapping memories, the associated (non-cued) memories are adaptively either strengthened or pruned/weakened depending on their relative associative strength with the shared element -- demonstrating that sleep-dependent memory reorganisation is a regulated, bidirectional process over a memory network's relational structure, not a uniform strengthening signal applied to everything reactivated.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-529 predicts that offline replay of non-contiguous episodes under a common evaluative frame drives SPLIT/MERGE/reweighting operations over equivalence classes -- reorganisation that can go in either direction (strengthen a valid grouping, weaken/split an invalid one) depending on the accumulated relational evidence, not a monotonic consolidation booster. Oyarzun et al. demonstrate exactly this bidirectionality in human sleep: reactivating one memory during sleep causes associated overlapping memories to be selectively strengthened OR weakened, adaptively, based on associative structure -- this is the clearest existing behavioral evidence that offline reorganisation is a genuinely RELATIONAL, bidirectional operation rather than uniform amplification, which is the core empirical signature MECH-529's split/merge framing needs. It equally supports ARC-137's taxonomy: bidirectional, adaptive restructuring of a memory network is a REORGANIZATION outcome, categorically distinct from simple retention/interference repair (uniform strengthening against decay) -- ARC-137's central claim that these are different offline OUTCOMES requiring different readouts is exactly what this paper's bidirectional signature (as opposed to a monotonic strengthening result) demonstrates.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The associative overlap structure here is explicitly taught via a paired-associate learning task with deliberately shared cue elements (an oracular, experimenter-supplied relational structure), not derived non-oracularly from accumulated consequential-divergence evidence the way MECH-529's mechanism specifies. This paper shows the FUNCTIONAL SIGNATURE (bidirectional, relationally-adaptive reorganisation) MECH-529 needs, without testing the specific non-oracular DERIVATION MECH-529 proposes for how that structure gets discovered in the first place.
mapping.source_context: Human behavioral study; healthy adult participants; paired-associate learning task with deliberately overlapping memory networks, targeted memory reactivation (TMR) during a nap as the causal manipulation, recall accuracy as the primary readout.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality, well-cited, causally-manipulated (TMR) peer-reviewed study in a strong venue -- this is the cleanest existing behavioral demonstration of bidirectional, relationally-adaptive offline memory reorganisation. Mapping fidelity is good for the functional signature (selective strengthen-or-weaken) MECH-529 needs; capped from higher by the oracular-structure gap shared with the Solomon 2026 entry in this same directory.
